spain/sierras-de-las-estancias-y-los-fil.text: A Spanish Vino de la Tierra indication in Andalusia, named after the Sierra de las Estancias and Sierra de los Filabres mountain ranges. It covers about 25 municipalities in Almería province and gained its status in 2008, one step below Denominación de Origen.

wiki.title: Sierras de las Estancias y los Filabres

spain/somontano.text: An Aragon appellation on the Pyrenean foothills, whose name means "beneath the mountain". Rules allow many grapes, including Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta, Moristel and Cabernet Sauvignon for red, and Chardonnay and Gewürztraminer for white. Wine production centers on the town of Barbastro.

spain/tarragona.text: A Catalan appellation in two separate areas, the Camp de Tarragona and the Ribera d'Ebre district. Rules allow wine, sparkling, liqueur and raisined-grape wines, from white Macabeo, Xarello and Parellada and reds such as Garnacha Tinta and Trepat.

spain/terra-alta.text: A Catalan appellation of 12 inland municipalities in the mountains of western Tarragona province, as its name "high land" suggests. Rules allow Garnacha Blanca, Garnacha Tinta, Macabeo and Syrah among others. It long made wine only for local use and only recently moved to modern Mediterranean styles.

spain/tierra-del-vino-de-zamora.text: A Zamora province appellation in Castile and León, upgraded to DOP status in 2007. Its rules cover wine from red Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta and Cabernet Sauvignon, and from white Verdejo, Godello, Albillo Mayor and Palomino.

wiki.title: Tierra del Vino de Zamora DO

spain/toro.text: A DOP in the southeast corner of Zamora province, in northwest Castile and León, with about 19,800 acres under vine. Its rules allow red Tempranillo and Garnacha Tinta, and white Verdejo, Doña Blanca, Albillo Real and Moscatel de Grano Menudo.

spain/ucles.text: A DOP in Castile-La Mancha, around the town of Uclés in western Cuenca and northeastern Toledo. Rules allow wine and quality sparkling wine from Tempranillo, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon and Garnacha Tinta, plus white Verdejo, Macabeo and Chardonnay.

spain/uruena.text: A one-commune DOP in Castile and León for wine from four red grapes: Tempranillo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah.

spain/utiel-requena.text: A DOP in Valencia province, named for the neighboring towns of Utiel and Requena and known for the predominant use of the Bobal grape. Rules also allow Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta, Macabeo and Merseguera, and sparkling and liqueur wines.

spain/val-do-salnes.text: A wine area within Rías Baixas, the Galician DO known for white wine from the Albariño grape. Rías Baixas also allows Godello, Loureira and Caíño Blanco for white, and Mencía, Espadeiro and Caíño Tinto for red.

spain/valdeorras.text: A DOP on the banks of the Sil river in the south of Ourense province, Galicia. Rules allow white Godello, Albariño, Loureira and Treixadura, and red Mencía, Brancellao and Sousón, as well as sparkling and raisined-grape wines.

spain/valdepenas.text: A DOP in the south of Castile-La Mancha, grouped with La Mancha as La Mancha & Valdepeñas. It is almost surrounded by the La Mancha DOP but separate because of its long history of a distinct style, aloque or clarete, made by mixing white and red grapes. Rules allow Tempranillo, Airén and Garnacha Tinta, among others.

spain/valencia.text: A DOP in Valencia province, split into two zones and four sub-zones that each make a different wine. Bobal is the most planted grape in the area, at 40 percent.

spain/valle-del-cinca.text: A Vino de la Tierra indication in the Cinca Valley, in Huesca province, Aragon. It covers about 15 municipalities and gained its status in 2005, one step below Denominación de Origen on the Spanish quality ladder.

spain/valle-del-mino-ourense.text: A Galician Vino de la Tierra indication in Ourense province. It covers six municipalities, including Ourense, Toén and Barbadás, and gained its status in 2001, one step below Denominación de Origen.

spain/vallegarcia.text: A single-estate Vino de Pago in Castilla-La Mancha, formed in 2019 and lying within the La Mancha DOP. Its rules allow wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Merlot, Petit Verdot and Syrah, with Viognier the only white grape.

spain/valles-de-benavente.text: A quality wine indication (Vino de Calidad con Indicación Geográfica) in northern Zamora province, Castile and León. Its rules allow red Tempranillo, Prieto Picudo, Mencía, Garnacha Tinta and Cabernet Sauvignon, and white Verdejo and Doña Blanca.

spain/valles-de-sadacia.text: A Vino de la Tierra indication in La Rioja that includes only white wines, in three styles: dry, semi-dry and sweet. It sits one step below Denominación de Origen on the Spanish quality ladder.

spain/valtiendas.text: A DOP of 16 communes whose rules allow wine from red Tempranillo, Garnacha Tinta, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Syrah, with Albillo Mayor the one white grape.

spain/vera-de-estenas.text: A single-estate Vino de Pago of the Vera de Estenas winery in Valencia, lying within the Utiel-Requena DOP. Its rules allow wine from Bobal, Tempranillo, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.

spain/vino-de-la-tierra-igp.text: Spain's group of regional wine indications, from Mallorca, Isla de Menorca and Formentera to Extremadura and Castilla.

spain/yecla.text: A DOP in the northernmost corner of Murcia, surrounded by Jumilla, Almansa and Alicante, and traditionally known as the home of Monastrell in Spain. It sells 92 percent of its wine abroad, the highest share of any Spanish DOP.

australia.text: One of the world's largest wine exporters, sending about 800 million of its 1.2 to 1.3 billion liters a year abroad. Wine is made in every state, and South Australia makes more than half. Syrah is the most planted grape at 30 percent, then Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay.

australia/adelaide.text: An Australian wine super zone in South Australia, the state that produces more than half of all Australian wine.

australia/adelaide-hills.text: A region in the hills east of Adelaide in South Australia, part of the Mount Lofty Ranges zone, with Lenswood and Piccadilly Valley inside it. Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay each make up 23 percent of plantings, followed by Pinot Noir at 18 percent.

australia/adelaide-plains.text: A South Australian region just north of Adelaide, in the Mount Lofty Ranges zone, with a GI since 2002. Syrah is 39 percent of plantings, followed by Cabernet Sauvignon at 14 percent.

australia/albany.text: A small subregion of Great Southern, Australia's largest wine region, in Western Australia, with about 200 acres of vines.

australia/alpine-valleys.text: A region in the North East Victoria zone, one of its five named wine regions, with no single leading grape. Chardonnay makes up 20 percent of plantings, Pinot Noir 16, Pinot Gris and Sauvignon Blanc 14 each, and Glera 11.

australia/barossa.text: A South Australian zone made up of two regions, Barossa Valley and Eden Valley. Syrah is 60 percent of plantings, with Cabernet Sauvignon at 14 percent and smaller shares of Grenache and Riesling.

australia/barossa-valley.text: A warm region about 35 miles northeast of Adelaide, in the Barossa zone of South Australia, founded by German settlers. Its warm continental climate gave very ripe grapes and an early fortified wine industry. Syrah is 65 percent of plantings, then Cabernet Sauvignon at 14 percent.

australia/beechworth.text: A small region in the North East Victoria zone, one of its five named wine regions, with about 310 acres of vines. Pinot Noir (22 percent) and Chardonnay (21) lead plantings, followed by Syrah (14) and Pinot Gris (10).

australia/bendigo.text: A region in Central Victoria where red grapes dominate plantings: Syrah is 44 percent, Cabernet Sauvignon 18 and Merlot 13. It covers a large area, with about 1,500 acres of vines.

australia/big-rivers.text: A large grape-growing zone covering the southwestern corner of New South Wales, with four regions: Murray Darling, Perricoota, Riverina and Swan Hill. Chardonnay is 38 percent of plantings and Syrah 20 percent.

australia/blackwood-valley.text: A region in the South West Australia area of Western Australia, with about 760 acres of vines. Sauvignon Blanc (26 percent), Syrah (22) and Cabernet Sauvignon (21) lead plantings, with Sémillon at 14 percent.

australia/broke-fordwich.text: A subregion of the Hunter Valley in New South Wales, with about 1,300 acres of vines.

australia/canberra-district.text: A cool-climate region around Canberra, in the Southern New South Wales zone, in a triangle with Yass, Bungendore and Murrumbateman as key places. Lower, inland parts near Yass are warmer than the high ground near Bungendore. Syrah is 32 percent of plantings, with Riesling at 12.

australia/central-ranges.text: A zone on the western slopes of the Great Dividing Range in central New South Wales, with three regions: Mudgee, Orange and Cowra. Syrah is 36 percent of plantings and Cabernet Sauvignon 27 percent.

australia/central-victoria.text: A large Victorian zone containing Bendigo, Goulburn Valley, Heathcote, Strathbogie Ranges and Upper Goulburn. Syrah dominates at 67 percent of plantings, with Chardonnay at 9 and Cabernet Sauvignon at 8.

australia/central-western-australia.text: A very small zone in Western Australia, with only about 100 acres of vines. Planting records for Peel show mostly Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon.

australia/clare-valley.text: One of Australia's oldest wine regions, in the Mount Lofty Ranges zone of South Australia's Mid North, about 88 miles north of Adelaide and best known for Riesling. Plantings are mostly Syrah (39 percent), with Cabernet Sauvignon at 22 and Riesling at 21.

australia/coonawarra.text: A South Australian region in the Limestone Coast, about 240 miles southeast of Adelaide, known for Cabernet Sauvignon grown on its terra rossa soil. Cabernet Sauvignon is 64 percent of plantings, with Syrah at 20 percent.

australia/cowra.text: The southernmost, lowest and warmest of the three Central Ranges regions in New South Wales, in the Lachlan River valley. Vines date from 1973 and are mostly irrigated white grapes. Chardonnay is 48 percent of plantings.

australia/currency-creek.text: A South Australian region on the west side of Lake Alexandrina, with a GI since 2001 and about 2,400 acres planted.

australia/denmark.text: A subregion of Great Southern, Australia's largest wine region, in Western Australia, with about 220 acres of vines.

australia/eastern-plains-inland-and-nort.text: A vast zone in Western Australia of about 913,000 square miles, with no vine area recorded. The state's wine regions are almost entirely in the cooler climate of its southwest tip.

australia/eden-valley.text: A South Australian region in the Mount Lofty Ranges, within the Barossa zone, from Truro in the north to just south of Springton, with a GI since 1997. High Eden lies inside it. Syrah is 36 percent of plantings and Riesling 23 percent.

australia/far-north.text: A huge zone in South Australia of about 331,000 square miles, with only about 430 acres of vines. The Southern Flinders Ranges lie inside it. South Australia as a whole makes more than half of all Australian wine.

australia/fleurieu.text: A South Australian zone with five regions inside it: Currency Creek, Kangaroo Island, Langhorne Creek, McLaren Vale and Southern Fleurieu. Syrah is 34 percent of plantings and Cabernet Sauvignon 25 percent.

australia/frankland-river.text: A subregion of Great Southern, Australia's largest wine region, in Western Australia, with about 3,300 acres of vines.

australia/geelong.text: A region in the Port Phillip area of Victoria where Pinot Noir leads plantings at 42 percent, ahead of Chardonnay (20) and Syrah (16). It has about 1,200 acres of vines.

australia/geographe.text: A region in the South West Australia area of Western Australia, with about 1,950 acres of vines and a mixed set of grapes: Syrah 21 percent, Sauvignon Blanc 19, Chardonnay 17, Cabernet Sauvignon 13 and Sémillon 11.

australia/gippsland.text: A large Victorian zone where Pinot Noir leads plantings at 38 percent, followed by Chardonnay (20) and Syrah (18). Vines cover only about 460 acres across a wide area, in a state with more wine producers than any other in Australia.

australia/glenrowan.text: A region in the North East Victoria zone, around Lake Mokoan, with vines first planted in 1866. Phylloxera hit in the 1890s, but vineyards were quickly replanted on resistant rootstocks. Syrah and Cabernet Sauvignon are each 32 percent of plantings.

australia/goulburn-valley.text: A Victorian region in the Central Victoria zone, with vineyards since 1860. Tahbilk still makes wine from vines planted in the 1860s, and sandy soil kept phylloxera out. Syrah is 29 percent of plantings, and Nagambie Lakes lies inside.

australia/grampians.text: A region in the Western Victoria area, west of Melbourne near the Grampians National Park, dominated by red wine, especially Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon. Syrah is 73 percent of plantings, and Great Western lies inside it.

australia/great-southern.text: Australia's largest wine region, about 120 miles east to west, in the South West Australia area of Western Australia. It is the coolest of the state's wine areas, with five subregions including Mount Barker and Frankland River. Syrah is 32 percent of plantings.

australia/great-western.text: A subregion of Grampians in the Western Victoria area, with about 1,200 acres of vines.

australia/greater-perth.text: A Western Australian zone containing Peel, Perth Hills and Swan District. Sauvignon Blanc leads plantings at 39 percent, followed by Chardonnay (17) and Cabernet Sauvignon (14). Western Australia makes less than 5 percent of the country's wine.

australia/gundagai.text: A New South Wales region in the Southern New South Wales zone, around Tumut, Cootamundra and Junee. Altitude ranges from about 690 to 1,050 feet. Syrah is 49 percent of plantings, with Chardonnay at 21 and Cabernet Sauvignon at 19.

australia/hastings-river.text: A small region in the Northern Rivers area of New South Wales, near Wauchope and Port Macquarie, within about 16 miles of the coast. Vines were first planted in 1837, and there was no wine production from 1920 to 1980. Sémillon is 38 percent of plantings.

australia/heathcote.text: A region in Central Victoria between Goulburn Valley and Bendigo, famous for its Shiraz. Syrah is 53 percent of plantings, with Chardonnay at 15 percent and smaller shares of Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache.

australia/henty.text: One of the cooler Australian regions, in the Western Victoria area in the southwest corner of the state, formerly called Drumborg. It is known for white Chardonnay, Riesling, Semillon and Sauvignon Blanc, though Pinot Noir is the most planted grape at 40 percent.

australia/high-eden.text: A subregion in the western, highest part of Eden Valley, within the Barossa zone of South Australia, at about 1,640 feet, registered in 2001. Its main grapes are Riesling, Cabernet Sauvignon, Shiraz and Chardonnay, and the cool, windy climate and poor soils give low yields.

australia/hilltops.text: A New South Wales region in the Southern New South Wales zone, around Boorowa, Harden and Young, with about 1,500 acres planted mostly to red grapes on dark red granitic clay with basalt, above 1,480 feet. Syrah is 43 percent of plantings and Cabernet Sauvignon 32 percent.

australia/hunter.text: A New South Wales region with Broke Fordwich, Pokolbin and Upper Hunter Valley inside it. It has about 6,400 acres of vines, mostly Syrah (29 percent), Chardonnay (25), Sémillon (16) and Verdelho (12).

australia/hunter-valley.text: One of Australia's first wine regions, in New South Wales, planted from the early 19th century. Known for Semillon, it also makes Shiraz, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon and Verdelho. The zone covers the whole catchment of the Hunter River.

australia/kangaroo-island.text: A South Australian region covering all of Kangaroo Island, in the Fleurieu area, with a GI since 2000. It has about 360 acres of vines, mostly Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon, with about 12 wineries in 2014.

australia/langhorne-creek.text: A region in South Australia's Fleurieu area, on the plains along the lower Bremer and Angas Rivers, reaching Lake Alexandrina, with a GI since 1998. Syrah is 39 percent of plantings and Cabernet Sauvignon 33 percent, across about 15,100 acres.

australia/lenswood.text: A small subregion of the Adelaide Hills in South Australia's Mount Lofty Ranges zone, with about 610 acres of vines.

australia/limestone-coast.text: A South Australian zone with six regions: Coonawarra, Mount Benson, Mount Gambier, Padthaway, Robe and Wrattonbully. Cabernet Sauvignon is 34 percent of plantings and Syrah 26 percent, followed by Merlot and Chardonnay at 10 percent each.

australia/lower-murray.text: A South Australian zone with Riverland inside it and about 55,000 acres of vines, covering a large area. South Australia as a whole makes more than half of all Australian wine.

australia/macedon-ranges.text: A region in the Port Phillip area of Victoria where Pinot Noir leads plantings at 35 percent, followed by Chardonnay (23) and Syrah (15). It has about 530 acres of vines.

australia/manjimup.text: A region in the South West Australia area of Western Australia where Merlot leads plantings at 38 percent, ahead of Sauvignon Blanc (15) and Chardonnay (12). It has about 380 acres of vines.

australia/margaret-river.text: A boutique-scale region in southwest Western Australia, in the South West Australia area, and the most maritime-influenced of the major Australian regions, with a Mediterranean pattern of rainfall. Cabernet Sauvignon is 26 percent of plantings, then Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Syrah and Sémillon.

australia/mclaren-vale.text: A South Australian region in the Fleurieu area, about 24 miles south of Adelaide, included in the Great Wine Capitals of the World. Syrah is 57 percent of plantings, with Cabernet Sauvignon at 18 percent and Grenache at 6 percent.

australia/mornington-peninsula.text: A cool-climate region south of Melbourne in Victoria's Port Phillip area, focused on Pinot Noir, with Chardonnay, Pinot Gris and Tempranillo too. Wines are medium bodied and dry, and sparkling wines show structure. Pinot Noir is 55 percent of plantings.

australia/mount-barker.text: A subregion of Great Southern, Australia's largest wine region, in Western Australia, with about 2,100 acres of vines.

australia/mount-benson.text: A South Australian region on the coast, about 190 miles from Adelaide between Kingston SE and Robe, and one of six in the Limestone Coast zone. It has about 1,300 acres of vines.

australia/mount-gambier.text: A young South Australian region in the Limestone Coast, first planted in 1982 and given a GI in 2010. It has about 670 acres of vines and, in 2014, eight wineries.

australia/mount-lofty-ranges.text: A South Australian zone containing Adelaide Hills, Adelaide Plains and Clare Valley, with about 23,600 acres of vines. South Australia as a whole makes more than half of all Australian wine.

australia/mudgee.text: A New South Wales region in the Central Ranges zone, with grapes grown since 1858 and large wineries replanting from 1974. It grows mostly red grapes, especially Shiraz, Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot.

australia/murray-darling.text: A large wine region in the Big Rivers zone with about 33,300 acres of vines, spanning the border of New South Wales and Victoria along the Murray River.

australia/nagambie-lakes.text: A subregion of Goulburn Valley in Central Victoria, around Lake Nagambie, with vineyards since 1860. Tahbilk still has vines from the 1860s. Key grapes are Shiraz, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Marsanne and Merlot, on well-draining iron oxide soil.

australia/new-england-australia.text: A large, thinly planted region in the Northern Slopes area of New South Wales, with only about 190 acres of vines.

australia/new-south-wales.text: An Australian state and the country's second-largest wine producer. Hunter Valley is its best-known region, but most production is in the Big Rivers zone, largely for box wine and mass brands. Across Big Rivers, Western Plains and Northern Slopes, Chardonnay and Syrah lead plantings.

australia/north-east-victoria.text: A Victorian zone with five regions: Alpine Valleys, Beechworth, Glenrowan, King Valley and Rutherglen. No grape dominates, with Merlot, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah each at 10 to 13 percent.

australia/north-west-victoria.text: A large Victorian zone of about 23,500 square miles, with about 21,400 acres of vines. Victoria has more wine producers than any other Australian state.

australia/northern-rivers.text: A New South Wales zone with Hastings River inside it and only about 340 acres of vines across about 16,700 square miles. Verdelho is the main recorded grape, at 14 percent.

australia/northern-slopes.text: A large New South Wales zone with New England Australia inside it and only about 280 acres of vines. Cabernet Sauvignon is 27 percent of plantings, followed by Syrah (18) and Sémillon (10).

australia/orange.text: A New South Wales region in the Central Ranges zone, defined as land above 2,000 feet, about 160 miles west of Sydney. Vines were first planted commercially in 1980. Syrah is 23 percent of plantings, followed by Chardonnay (18).

australia/padthaway.text: A region in the Limestone Coast zone of southeast South Australia, along the Riddoch Highway, with a GI since 1999 and about 10,000 acres of vines. Syrah is 31 percent of plantings, Cabernet Sauvignon 28 and Chardonnay 20.

australia/peel.text: A region in the Greater Perth zone of Western Australia, with only about 130 acres of vines. Syrah is 33 percent of plantings and Cabernet Sauvignon 25 percent, followed by Verdelho and Chardonnay.

australia/pemberton.text: A region in the South West Australia area of Western Australia where Sauvignon Blanc is 48 percent of plantings, followed by Chardonnay at 26 percent. It has about 1,200 acres of vines.

australia/perricoota.text: A region in the Big Rivers zone of New South Wales, with about 1,000 acres of vines, planted mostly to Merlot (31 percent), Petite Sirah (20) and Cabernet Sauvignon (18). Big Rivers has four regions, including Murray Darling and Riverina.

australia/perth-hills.text: A region in the Greater Perth zone of Western Australia, with about 290 acres of vines. Syrah is 37 percent of plantings, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay at 11 percent each.

australia/piccadilly-valley.text: A small subregion of the Adelaide Hills in South Australia's Mount Lofty Ranges zone, with about 550 acres of vines.

australia/pokolbin.text: A subregion within the Hunter Valley in New South Wales, with about 3,300 acres of vines.

australia/porongurup.text: A small subregion of Great Southern, Australia's largest wine region, in Western Australia, with about 240 acres of vines.

australia/port-phillip.text: A Victorian zone containing Geelong, Macedon Ranges, Mornington Peninsula, Sunbury and Yarra Valley. Syrah is 36 percent of plantings, Cabernet Sauvignon 26 and Merlot 15, with Pinot Noir at 9 percent.

australia/pyrenees.text: A region in the Western Victoria area, around the Pyrenees ranges and the town of Avoca, at the southern end of the Great Dividing Range. Hills rise from about 980 to over 2,460 feet. Syrah is 36 percent of plantings, followed by Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon.
